Follow-up after emergency visit
Ms. Roe presented to the emergency department on 2026-02-09 with sudden weakness of the left arm
and slurred speech, which resolved completely within 30 minutes. Neurological examination at this visit is
normal.
MRI brain on 2026-02-10: no acute infarct, no hemorrhage, no intracranial metastases.
Assessment: transient ischemic attack on 2026-02-09. Started aspirin 81 mg daily and atorvastatin. Plan:
carotid ultrasound; return immediately for new symptoms.

SYNTHETIC PATIENT - FICTIONAL DATA - FOR DEMONSTRATION ONLY

Pulmonology consultation

Patient ID: SYN-004

Document date: 2025-05-06

Consultation summary

Ms. Roe is seen in follow-up for a respiratory illness. In March 2025 she developed dry cough and exertional dyspnea while receiving FOLFOX for colorectal cancer. CT chest showed bilateral ground-glass and reticular opacities. Infection was excluded, and she was diagnosed with drug-induced interstitial pneumonitis, felt to be oxaliplatin-related. Oxaliplatin was permanently discontinued and she completed a prednisone taper in April 2025. She is now asymptomatic. Plan: avoid oxaliplatin; repeat pulmonary function tests in one year.
